newsitem.title: TANZANIA: DHL to double Tanzania-Nairobi capacity.
newsitem.headline: DHL to double Tanzania-Nairobi capacity.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express plans to double cargo capacity on its charter flight between the Tanzanian capital and Nairobi due to growing business, DHL Tanzania Ltd managing director, Max Shaw said on Monday.

"Now we have a daily charted twin-engine Cessna with a capacity of about 500 kilogramme, but we are working at getting a Cessna with a capacity of 1,000 to 1,500 kilogramme. We hope to get that started soon," Shaw told Reuters in an interview.

"Our daily charter flight from Dar Es Salaam to Nairobi provides an opportunity to deliver to London within 24 hours from Tanzania. There is a growing market here for both freight and air express and it's getting more competitive," he said.
DHL opened up for business in Tanzania in 1989 following the government's launch of economic market-orientated reforms in the mid-1980s after a 20-year period with socialist-type policies.

Since the first office was opened in Dar-es-Salaam DHL has opened two more branches in the capital in addition to provincial operations in western Mwanza, northern Arusha and Moshi, north eastern Tanga, central Morogoro and at the clove and spices island of Zanzibar.

Mwanza is the centre of Tanzania's rapidly growing mining industry while Moshi is the country's most important coffee-growing region and Arusha is home to Tanzania's biggest tourist attractions, Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti National Park.
Tanzania, following the example of neighbouring Kenya, is also seeing a fast growing horticulture industry in fertile areas around Arusha which is dominated by Dutch and Israeli flower growers.

"The East Africa (airfreight) market is growing tremendously. Nairobi is basically the East African hub, but Tanzania has seen a steady growth and even Kampala in Uganda is getting quite important for us," Shaw said.
He said DHL already was planning to open new branch offices in the southern Mbeya region and central Iringa in order to cope with the increasing demand for air express service.
"In the first five years of operation we had a pretty dramatic growth. The biggest growth has been seen on the domestic market. It (Tanzania) is a market which slowly starts to mature.

"Tanzania is becoming more and more part of the international ecomony as the country is opening up, while regional trade is growing dramatically, both within the East African market as well as to South Africa," said Shaw. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
